**me (20:51):** Simply:

**Take the candle's wick — the low in a downmove, the high in an upmove — and it has to land in this band:**

```
                    ↑  1.0 ATR ABOVE the node   ← may stop this far short
        ═══════ NODE ═══════
                    ↓  1.5 ATR BELOW the node   ← may poke this far through
```

Downmove: the **low** must be no more than 1 ATR above the node and no more than 1.5 ATR below it. Upmove: mirror it on the **high** — no more than 1 ATR below, no more than 1.5 ATR above.

Asymmetric on purpose: tight on the approach, loose through it, because a stab that pokes through and recovers is still a test.

In actual SPY points, since ATR(14) on 3-min runs ~0.38:

| | short of node | through node |
|---|---|---|
| typical day (ATR 0.38) | 0.38 | 0.57 |
| quiet (ATR 0.25) | 0.25 | 0.38 |
| volatile open (ATR 0.75) | 0.75 | 1.13 |

So on a normal day it's roughly **0.40 above, 0.55 below** — call it half a point either way, widening when the tape speeds up.

Two things that go with it and matter as much as the numbers: use the **wick** for this test but the **close** to decide whether it deflected or broke, and count **one price event as one deflection** — never once per node, or overlapping nodes double-count it.

  `tapeMap` and applied `!fromFeed` (v14.15). Two computations of one quantity - which DECISIONS
  v13.2 already forbade. **The export now reads the face's array.**

  bought a MISSING level, not a safer one.

- ⚠ **`file://` WORKS IN IRT'S REMOTE FILE FIELD.** The 2026-08-27 conclusion ("IRT does not poll a
  local file") was true of LOCAL FILE mode only; the inference that HTTP was therefore required was
  wrong. The python server is retired to a fallback and is now IN GIT (`tools/irt/`) - it had existed
  only as chat attachments, which is why a later context reported it never built.
- ⚠ **OVERLAY = GEX is the fifth required-posture rule.** GEX+VEX blends the LADDER (7750 read 57%
  vs 68%). `tapeMapLive` already defended the rail by falling back to the gamma feed; the QQQ export
  did not, and that is what the operator saw.

### DECISIONS

- **THE FEATURE WAS RE-POSED TWICE, AND THAT IS WHAT MADE IT WORK.** "Where will the HOD print" is
  unanswerable (F-13). "Will price REACH this level" is AUC 0.826 and calibrated (F-14). "GIVEN it
  reaches it, when" is AUC 0.692 (F-15). Same data, three questions, two of them useful.
- ⚠⚠ **THE SHIPPED 92% IN CALL IS 63% IN REAL TIME (F-12).** The study behind it picked the side
  WITH HINDSIGHT, so every failed call was relabelled out of the sample. The CELL rate on the face
  is honest (says 70-79%, happens 75%); the DECISION figure in the hover is not. Still to correct.
- ⚠ **A SPARSE CONTROL NEARLY SHIPPED A PHANTOM (F-16):** prior-day levels "worth +12 points" of
  touch probability, which vanished entirely under a dense distance control. Recorded because the
  near-miss is worth more than the answer - and because that same test IS the gamma experiment.
- **HIS 80% / 30-MINUTE ASK IS NOT AVAILABLE AND THE FACE SAYS SO.** A +-15-minute box lands 15% of
  the time; 80% needs a 3.6-hour window. Shipped as a one-sided FLOOR at 80% plus the middle-half
  window at its true 50%, with the arithmetic printed under it.
- **THE LADDER WAS DELETED** - the same evidence as the verdict, a weaker instrument (age alone AUC
  0.818 vs 0.879), and visibly disagreeing with it on his own screenshot (74% above, 41% below).
- **THE FORECAST-VOCABULARY BAN IS NOW SCOPED BY THE SOURCE ITSELF** (`PROB-BLOCK-START/END`) and is
  STRICTER inside it: "likely" may not appear without a percentage. DECISIONS D-12 predicted exactly
  this would be needed the moment a probability feature shipped.
- **ATR: NO. Overnight: NO. Volume, IB30, day-of-week, gap, prior-day/overnight level identity: NO.**
  Sixteen factors, one pass each, all recorded so they are not re-proposed.


### SHIPPED

**v14.79** - the far-side block (three levels x P(trades there) x first-passage timing), the timing
line (80% floor / 50% window / hazard), the ladder and the honesty line removed, the honesty content
moved into the header hover with `rates live` left visible, `farside` ENROLLED with node identity in
its record (the gamma data nobody has ever collected), companion **v1.16** couriering FARSIDE.json
and two years of daily ^VIX, `tools/study-farside.py` deriving every table the panel carries, and
`test_farside.js` - 30 executed assertions, six mutations, six distinct failures. Suite 119 green.

  60 minutes of every session because the study required IB60 to exist first. IB60 was measured
  WORTHLESS and dropped from the model in the same session — **the exclusion stayed behind**.
  Re-derived from minute 5: 72/72 cells, and AUC on the SAME late rows is IDENTICAL (0.8787), so it
  is strictly additive. ⚠ **Grep the study for every assumption a deleted feature justified.**
- **THE NOT-IN CALL LIVED IN THE MISSING CELLS:** 72% on n=85 at 09:45 became **85% on n=230 at
  08:40**. The better half of the feature had been excluded by a leftover.
- **TWO TESTS WERE COUPLED TO DATA, NOT LOGIC.** They used the empty 08:30 column as the fixture for
  "a thin cell refuses"; filling the table broke them. They inject a thin cell now. ⚠ A test that
  passes because of what the data happens to contain is not testing the code.
- **THE IRT EXPORT IS WORKING** — verified live (how:file, inPlace:true, err:null, both Kings on
  EPU26). Only two rows because emPiles has no band anchor: the same F-10 chain. Expect it to fill
  once bars anchor the band.

### DECISIONS

- **localStorage WAS FULL — ONE FAULT, SIX SYMPTOMS.** Measured 10,240 KB = exactly Chrome's cap
  (`gpts_recorder_v7` 5,957 KB for ONE day, `gpts_nodeevents_v1` 3,228 KB); a 40 KB probe threw
  QuotaExceededError. Every setItem had been failing behind `catch(e){}` for a week. It produced:
  the feature-record collapse, the corpus tap "never running", the base-rate courier never
  delivering, IF levels 8.5h stale, a wrong conclusion that the companion was on v1.14 — and
  **the blank pre-open rail**, because `lastBookSave()` could never write `gpts_lastbook_v1`, so the
  band has had no prior close to anchor on. FINDINGS F-10.
- ⚠ **A DIAGNOSTIC CREATED ITS OWN EVIDENCE.** Deleting two keys to test "is the companion alive"
  freed just enough room for the tiny calendar object to write — which looked like proof the script
  ran and only Yahoo was broken. It sent me to the wrong conclusion twice.
- ⚠ **THE v14.67 INSTRUMENT WAS AIMED AT THE WRONG LAYER.** FEATH counters asked registry-vs-dedupe.
  Neither: records were built correctly every bar and discarded at the final setItem. **One quota
  check would have found in 30 seconds what a night of reasoning did not.**
- **HE WILL INSTALL DURING THE TRADING DAY**, so the build was split by INSTALL RISK, not effort:
  display and read-only hooks ship now; anything touching `recorderSave()` waits for the close.
  The bounded-write work is parked at `session-state/pending/v14.68-bounded-writes.patch` rather
  than discarded.
- **THE ±5pt EM CLIPPING COULD NOT BE MEASURED** — it needs live RTH and the session had not opened.
  ⚠ But `dte0 EM = 42.3 pts` reads correctly, which already contradicts the note's hypothesis (a)
  that the EM is a SPY straddle applied unconverted. Re-measure before believing that note.

than an estimate, with a verdict that names `gpts_nodeevents_v1` as the safe mid-session clear and
`gpts_recorder_v7` as never-during-RTH. Read-only; safe to install while trading.

  helper `fh()` did the same. Each ADDED a new way for a bar to record nothing - the exact bug being
  investigated. Now a self-contained try/catch per counter.
- **`registerCoreFeatures()` WAS CALLED UNGUARDED** inside featRecordAll, so a throw there killed the
  bar's whole record silently. Now caught and counted. Its guard is `if(FEATURES.length) return` -
  "did ANY register", not "did all 47" - so a partial registry would be permanent. Healthy at 47 on
  the live panel tonight, but it had to be ruled out with a counter, not an argument.

### DECISIONS

- **HE ASKED ME TO SANITY-CHECK THE APPROACH AND IT DID NOT SURVIVE.** The 5-feature logistic was
  measured against a plain 2-axis lookup: AUC 0.8795 vs 0.8787, **identical Brier 0.1321**. The
  regression was ceremony. **The table ships** - same accuracy, every cell carries its n, and it can
  be argued with. Adding a third axis made it worse (thin cells). This is the operator's own standing
  instruction - *"why are you making things more complicated"* - arriving as a measurement.
- **THE SURVIVAL FRAMING WAS WORTH TESTING AND IS WORSE.** A discrete-time hazard model is the
  textbook fit for "will a new extreme print before the close": AUC 0.8751, Brier 0.1464 against the
  classifier's 0.8795 / 0.1321. Classification was right - but it had been an ASSUMPTION until then.
- **I STATED A FEAR AND IT WAS WRONG.** The worry was that the table is most confident only once the
  move is over, since its confidence comes from posr. Measured (F-5): at the 70% call, **half the
  range is still ahead** and price travels a median 30% of it. Recorded because stating the fear
  before testing it is what made the test happen.
- **THE OPERATING POINT IS 70%, PICKED BY THE DATA.** Below it the edge over the clock is thin; above
  it, time and forgone travel cost more than the accuracy gained.
- **BOTH DIVERGENCES AND SWEEPS ARE OUT, ON EVIDENCE.** Sweeps 48% (below their own base rate),
  momentum divergence 0.545, NQ cross-market -0.0014. ⚠ SWP had been rendering as a CONFIRMATION on
  ⓪a since v14.57; its hover now carries the 48%.
- **A TEST CAUGHT A SILENT RENDER BUG.** `lodhodCall` set `out.left`; the render and the test read
  `CALL.far`. The "% still ahead" would never have drawn. Found by an assertion that EXECUTES the
  function - a grep for `left` would have passed.
- **AND A MUTATION CAUGHT A TEST THAT COULD NOT FAIL** - nothing asserted that a thin cell refuses.
  Fifth occurrence of that pattern in this project.

### DECISIONS

- **HE DEFINED THE FIVE PENDING FIELDS, AND THE TAPE CONFIRMED THEM.** BOP/WICK/W.END/WICK%/MUD had
  been printed as PENDING since v14.57 because no definition existed anywhere. He supplied Wick%
  (*"the percentage of the total range"*) and the rest were DERIVED from his own printed numbers,
  then verified bar-by-bar on the live ES tape for 2026-08-27. The two fields that do not depend on
  extremity timing matched EXACTLY - **Wick% 26 vs 26, W.End 8:42am vs 8:42am**. The other three
  land within the 1-2 minute ES=F-vs-EPM26 offset that DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md predicts, which is the
  provenance warning proving itself useful rather than theoretical.
- **W.END IS A CLOSE, NOT A TOUCH.** First touch of the open was 8:41, first close 8:42; his panel
  prints 8:42. One session decided that, and it is written down as such.
- **WICK% IS A PRICE RATIO, ESTABLISHED BY ELIMINATION.** No duration ratio can produce 26%
  (wick/session 3.1%, wick/gap 5.6%). That was the reasoning that let me ask him one precise
  question instead of five vague ones.
- **HIS EXCLUSION RULE:** *"if there is no wick, then its 0 ... these days should not be averaged.
  also crazy outliers should not be averaged."* So a zero wick PRINTS 0 on the day's own row and is
  excluded from the medians, and outliers are fenced by **Tukey 1.5xIQR computed from the corpus** -
  a threshold derived from the data rather than a number I chose. Every exclusion is COUNTED into
  BASERATES.json so the n on the face is the n behind the number.
- **NEVER RECLAIMING THE OPEN IS NOT ZERO - IT IS UNKNOWN.** A session that never closes back
  through the open has no completed wick; printing 0 would claim the excursion ended instantly, the
  opposite of what happened. Those render em-dash. Building the test fixture for it taught me the
  case is narrower than it looks: it needs the LOD first, the high afterwards, and no close back
  through the open all day.
- **I ASKED A BAD QUESTION.** He replied *"i dont know what you are asking me"* - I had framed a
  refusal-rule question in my own vocabulary instead of asking what the field meant. The answer was
  simpler than the question. **Ask in his terms.**
- **A FIFTH NAME COLLISION.** `dropped` in the new Tukey loop shadowed the incomplete-session list
  built forty lines above, and `len(dropped)` exploded. GREP BEFORE NAMING.

  reader, never the front door, or it would re-latch its own output every tick and never age out.
